## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahāsaṅgāma* ("The Great Chapter on the Resolution of Conflicts") is the fifteenth chapter of the *Parivāra*, the final collection of the Vinaya Piṭaka. The text sets forth the rules, procedures, and requirements to be observed when a monastic addresses or speaks on matters of conflict (*adhikaraṇa*) before the Saṅgha. As discussed in secondary monastic legal manuals, the chapter establishes that disputes may be adjudicated by a complete Saṅgha, an assembled group (*gaṇa*, such as an *ubbāhikā* committee), or a single senior individual (*puggala* / *saṅghathera*), depending on the gravity of the matter [Entrance to the Vinaya Vol. 3 1983].
